attempts.summary: Set up btrfs-backed filesystem snapshotting for /srv/data on node1 (RHEL7; no LVM, rsync, or yum repos available, so used btrfs which was already present via btrfs-progs + a loadable kernel module). Created a loop-backed btrfs image persistently mounted at /srv/data (subvol=current) via /etc/fstab (nofail), populated application data, took a read-only snapshot (snapshots/baseline), modified the live data (edited a config file, deleted a file, added a new file), then restored by deleting the 'current' subvolume and recreating it as a writable snapshot of 'baseline' — verified via SHA-256 manifest diff that restored content matched the original snapshot exactly. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and data/mount health baseline, issued systemctl reboot (ack returned before disconnect), polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified /srv/data auto-remounted with both btrfs subvolumes intact and data checksums identical to the pre-restart baseline.
